verdict.rationale: Obsidian ships an official TypeScript Plugin API (documented, hosted on GitHub) with interfaces like Vault, plus a URI protocol for triggering actions and a headless Sync client explicitly aimed at 'CI pipelines, agents, and automated workflows,' giving AI-native builders a real, documented surface to build against. However there's no first-party AI/agent-specific SDK (e.g., REST API, Python/Node client), and community evidence notes plugins run with full filesystem/network access with no sandboxing, which is a security caveat for agentic use rather than a capability gap. missing for 10: dedicated AI-agent SDK/REST API, independent hands-on confirmation of headless-sync-for-agents working end-to-end, sandboxed execution model for agent-run plugins.
